```{r}
#| include: false
library(targets); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
ph_all <- tar_read(ph_data)
ph <- ph_all |> filter(qc_in_range) |> mutate(year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")), month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")))
q <- \(x, p) quantile(x, p, names = FALSE)
r2 <- \(x) round(x, 2)
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
cols <- c("old buoy" = "#8c8c8c", "new buoy" = "#1f78b4")

# Download files (the website `resources` copies downloads/ into the site)
dir.create("downloads", showWarnings = FALSE)
# Raw sub-daily pH (target `ph_raw`), times in NZST (UTC+12)
ph_raw <- tar_read(ph_raw)
ph_raw |> arrange(datetime, depth_m) |> mutate(datetime = format(datetime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "Etc/GMT-12")) |>
  write.csv("downloads/rotorua_ph_timeseries.csv", row.names = FALSE)

prof <- tar_read(buoy_profile_daily)

alk <- tar_read(alk_data) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(datetime), site = ifelse(grepl("^EK", site_id), "Site 2", "Site 5"),
         sample = c(DIS = "Discrete", INT = "Integrated", HYP = "Hypolimnion")[sub(".*_", "", site_id)])
tar_read(alk_data) |> arrange(datetime, site_id) |> mutate(datetime = format(datetime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")) |>
  write.csv("downloads/rotorua_alkalinity_hardness_doc.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## The data

pH is measured by the Lake Rotorua monitoring buoy and enters the model workflow as `CHM_ph` (see `R/format_buoy_for_aeme.R`). It is used to check the pH response (`fpH`) of the alum module, and is an input to the [alum calibration](alum-calibration-stage-1.qmd). The record is two buoy deployments with different sensor set-ups:

- **Old buoy**: a fixed sensor at 1 m logging every 15 minutes, 25 Feb 2014 to 7 Jan 2018 (only 4 days in 2018).
- **New buoy**: a profiler that logs about every 2.5 minutes while moving through 1 to 21 m, 21 Feb 2022 to 17 Sep 2026.
- The inventory and analysis below use the daily means in 0.5 m depth bins that go into the model workflow (targets `old_buoy_wq`, `aeme_buoy_data` and `ph_data`); the download is the raw data (target `ph_raw`).
- There is **no pH record between January 2018 and February 2022**.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Inventory of the daily-mean pH record. The quantiles use values between 4 and 11 only."
i <- ph_all |> group_by(source) |> summarise(n = n(), n_out = sum(!qc_in_range), first = min(date), last = max(date), days = n_distinct(date),
  depth_min = min(depth_m), depth_max = max(depth_m), n_depths = n_distinct(depth_m), median = r2(median(ph[qc_in_range])),
  p05 = r2(q(ph[qc_in_range], .05)), p95 = r2(q(ph[qc_in_range], .95)), min = r2(min(ph)), max = r2(max(ph))) |> arrange(desc(source))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Source = i$source, `Values` = format(i$n, big.mark = ","), `Days` = i$days, First = i$first, Last = i$last,
  `Depths (m)` = paste0(i$depth_min, "–", i$depth_max, " (", i$n_depths, ")"), Median = i$median, `5th–95th pct` = paste(i$p05, i$p95, sep = "–"),
  Min = i$min, Max = i$max, `Out of range` = i$n_out, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Quality control.** Only `r sum(!ph_raw$qc_in_range)` of the `r format(nrow(ph_raw), big.mark = ",")` raw values are outside the plausible range of 4 to 11, and they are flagged `qc_in_range = FALSE` in the download rather than removed. All figures and tables on this page exclude them (in the daily means, this leaves a single flagged value of 12.7 at 14.5 m on 2024-05-28). The old buoy record has a minimum of 5.2 and the new buoy of 5.3 (at 20 m in February 2025); these are plausible for the anoxic hypolimnion but have not been checked against grab samples. The two sensors have not been cross-calibrated.

## Time series

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-ts
#| fig-cap: "Daily median pH in the surface layer (<= 5 m), old and new buoy."
#| out-width: "90%"
ph |> filter(depth_m <= 5) |> group_by(source, date) |> summarise(ph = median(ph), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, ph, colour = source)) + geom_point(size = .5, alpha = .5) + scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "pH (daily median, <= 5 m)", colour = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Annual summaries (all depths). Fractions are of all values in the year."
y <- ph |> group_by(source, year) |> summarise(days = n_distinct(date), median = r2(median(ph)), p05 = r2(q(ph, .05)), p95 = r2(q(ph, .95)),
  frac_gt8 = r2(mean(ph > 8)), frac_lt65 = r2(mean(ph < 6.5)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Source = y$source, Year = y$year, Days = y$days, Median = y$median, `5th pct` = y$p05, `95th pct` = y$p95,
  `Fraction > 8` = y$frac_gt8, `Fraction < 6.5` = y$frac_lt65, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

- **pH is typically near neutral.** The median is 6.95 (old buoy) and 6.83 (new buoy), with 90% of values between about 6.1 and 7.8.
- **2022 and 2023 were higher** (median 7.4) than 2024 (6.8) and 2025 (6.5). In 2025, 51% of values were below 6.5. 2026 has partly recovered (6.8, to September).
- **Caution:** part of the 2023 to 2025 fall could be sensor drift rather than a real change. This has not been tested against independent measurements.

## Depth structure

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-depth
#| fig-cap: "Depth profile of pH, old and new buoy combined: median (line), interquartile range (dark band) and 5th to 95th percentile (light band) at each 0.5 m depth."
#| out-width: "60%"
#| fig-height: 5.5
pd <- ph |> group_by(depth_m) |> summarise(med = median(ph), p05 = q(ph, .05), p25 = q(ph, .25), p75 = q(ph, .75), p95 = q(ph, .95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pd, aes(y = depth_m)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(xmin = p05, xmax = p95), orientation = "y", fill = "#b2df8a", alpha = .5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(xmin = p25, xmax = p75), orientation = "y", fill = "#33a02c", alpha = .5) +
  geom_path(aes(x = med), linewidth = .8) + scale_y_reverse() + labs(x = "pH", y = "Depth (m)") + th
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "pH by depth class."
d <- ph |> mutate(depth_class = as.character(cut(depth_m, c(-1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 25, 40)))) |> group_by(depth_class) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median = r2(median(ph)), p05 = r2(q(ph, .05)), p95 = r2(q(ph, .95)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Depth class (m)` = d$depth_class, n = format(d$n, big.mark = ","), Median = d$median, `5th pct` = d$p05, `95th pct` = d$p95, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

pH decreases with depth: a median of 7.1 in the upper 5 m against 6.7 at 15 to 21 m (only the new buoy measures below 1 m), consistent with respiration and CO₂ accumulation in the stratified bottom water. The surface layer shows the high values (the 95th percentile is 8.2) that come with photosynthesis in summer blooms.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-zones
#| fig-cap: "Monthly median pH in the surface (<= 5 m), mid (5 to 17 m) and bottom (>= 17 m) layers."
#| out-width: "90%"
ph |> mutate(zone = ifelse(depth_m <= 5, "Surface (<= 5 m)", ifelse(depth_m >= 17, "Bottom (>= 17 m)", "Mid (5-17 m)")),
             ym = as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))) |> group_by(zone, ym) |> summarise(ph = median(ph), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(ym, ph, colour = zone)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = .8) + labs(x = NULL, y = "pH (monthly median)", colour = NULL) +
  th + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Seasonality

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-seasonal
#| fig-cap: "Monthly distributions of surface (<= 5 m) pH, both buoys combined."
#| out-width: "70%"
ggplot(filter(ph, depth_m <= 5), aes(factor(month), ph)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .3, fill = "#a6cee3") + labs(x = "Month", y = "pH (<= 5 m)") + th
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Surface (<= 5 m) pH by month."
m <- ph |> filter(depth_m <= 5) |> group_by(month) |> summarise(n = n(), median = r2(median(ph)), p05 = r2(q(ph, .05)), p95 = r2(q(ph, .95)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Month = month.abb[m$month], n = format(m$n, big.mark = ","), Median = m$median, `5th pct` = m$p05, `95th pct` = m$p95, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

The seasonal cycle of the median is weak (6.9 to 7.3). The spread is what changes: the 95th percentile exceeds 8.3 in December to March and in September (summer productivity) and the 5th percentile is lowest in February and April (6.1).

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-hist
#| fig-cap: "Density of all pH values (0.1 pH bins), by buoy."
#| out-width: "60%"
ggplot(ph, aes(ph, fill = source)) + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = .1, position = "identity", alpha = .6) + scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = "pH", y = "Density", fill = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Relationship with other profiler variables

The profiler measures temperature, fluorescence chlorophyll, dissolved oxygen, ORP, turbidity and specific conductance alongside pH (target `buoy_profile_daily`: daily means in 0.5 m bins, 2022 to 2026, so the new buoy only). The old buoy has no chlorophyll record. Chlorophyll here is in-situ fluorescence (`FlChlr`), which is not calibrated against lab chlorophyll-a, so it is a relative index of phytoplankton.

```{r}
#| include: false
vars <- c(`Temperature` = "temp_c", `Chlorophyll (fluorescence)` = "chl_fl", `DO (mg/L)` = "do_mgl", `DO saturation (%)` = "do_sat",
          `ORP` = "orp_mv", `Turbidity` = "turb", `Specific conductance` = "spcond", `Depth` = "depth_m")
sp <- \(x, y) suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
prof <- prof |> mutate(zone = cut(depth_m, c(0, 5, 10, 17, 22), labels = c("0-5 m", "5-10 m", "10-17 m", "17-22 m")))
# anomalies from the long-term mean at each depth (removes the average depth gradient)
anom <- prof |> group_by(depth_m) |> mutate(across(c(ph, temp_c, chl_fl, do_mgl, do_sat, orp_mv, turb, spcond), \(x) x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |> ungroup()
cr <- data.frame(Variable = names(vars),
  All = sapply(vars, \(v) sp(prof$ph, prof[[v]])),
  sapply(levels(prof$zone), \(z) sapply(vars, \(v) sp(prof$ph[prof$zone == z], prof[[v]][prof$zone == z]))),
  `Anomaly from depth mean` = sapply(vars, \(v) if (v == "depth_m") NA else sp(anom$ph, anom[[v]])), check.names = FALSE)
cr[-1] <- lapply(cr[-1], r2)
rownames(cr) <- NULL
g <- \(v, z) cr[cr$Variable == v, z]
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Spearman rank correlation of daily mean pH (0.5 m bins) with the other profiler variables: all depths, by depth zone, and for anomalies from each depth's long-term mean."
knitr::kable(cr)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ph-corr
#| fig-cap: "pH against fluorescence chlorophyll and temperature by depth zone. Points are daily means at 0.5 m (chlorophyll above its 99.5th percentile omitted); lines are linear fits."
#| out-width: "95%"
#| fig-height: 6
long <- prof |> filter(chl_fl < quantile(chl_fl, .995, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(chl_fl, temp_c), names_to = "var", values_to = "x") |>
  mutate(var = c(chl_fl = "Chlorophyll (fluorescence)", temp_c = "Temperature (°C)")[var])
ggplot(long, aes(x, ph)) + geom_point(size = .2, alpha = .15, colour = "grey30") + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#e31a1c", linewidth = .7) +
  facet_grid(zone ~ var, scales = "free_x") + labs(x = NULL, y = "pH") + th
```

- **Oxygen is the strongest correlate** (Spearman `r g("DO saturation (%)", "All")` with saturation and `r g("DO (mg/L)", "All")` with concentration over all depths; `r g("DO saturation (%)", "0-5 m")` for saturation in the top 5 m and `r g("DO saturation (%)", "17-22 m")` at 17 to 22 m). Both pH and oxygen respond to the balance of photosynthesis and respiration, so this is expected and not independent evidence.
- **Chlorophyll is positively correlated with pH** (`r g("Chlorophyll (fluorescence)", "All")` overall, from `r g("Chlorophyll (fluorescence)", "0-5 m")` in the top 5 m to `r g("Chlorophyll (fluorescence)", "17-22 m")` at 17 to 22 m). It stays at `r g("Chlorophyll (fluorescence)", "Anomaly from depth mean")` after removing each depth's mean, so days with more chlorophyll have higher pH at a given depth.
- **Temperature is negatively correlated overall** (`r g("Temperature", "All")`), but the relationship changes with depth: `r g("Temperature", "0-5 m")` in the top 5 m and `r g("Temperature", "17-22 m")` at 17 to 22 m, where colder water has the higher pH.
- **Turbidity and specific conductance** have correlations of `r g("Turbidity", "All")` and `r g("Specific conductance", "All")` with pH over all depths, and ORP (`r g("ORP", "All")`) largely follows oxygen.
- These are rank correlations of autocorrelated daily data from one site. They show association only, and any significance test would be overstated.

## Alkalinity, hardness and dissolved organic carbon

Discrete lake samples from Sites 2 and 5 (target `alk_data`, from the BOPRC file `alkalinity, tot hardness & diss org Carbon.xlsx`) give the buffering context for the pH record. Alkalinity and total hardness are in mg/L as CaCO₃; DOC is in g/m³ (the same as mg/L).

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Inventory of the alkalinity, total hardness and DOC samples by site and sample type."
inv <- alk |> group_by(Site = site, `Sample type` = sample) |> summarise(
  First = min(date), Last = max(date), `Alkalinity (n)` = sum(!is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3)), `Hardness (n)` = sum(!is.na(hardness_mgl_caco3)), `DOC (n)` = sum(!is.na(doc_gm3)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(inv)
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the three variables (alkalinity and hardness in mg/L as CaCO₃, DOC in g/m³), all sites and sample types."
sm <- \(x, nm) data.frame(Variable = nm, n = sum(!is.na(x)), Min = r2(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), Median = r2(median(x, na.rm = TRUE)), Max = r2(max(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
knitr::kable(rbind(sm(alk$alkalinity_mgl_caco3, "Alkalinity"), sm(alk$hardness_mgl_caco3, "Total hardness"), sm(alk$doc_gm3, "DOC")), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-alk-ts
#| fig-cap: "Alkalinity at Sites 2 and 5 (lines and filled points: integrated samples; hollow points: discrete and hypolimnion samples)."
#| out-width: "90%"
ggplot(alk |> filter(!is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3)), aes(date, alkalinity_mgl_caco3, colour = site, shape = sample == "Integrated")) +
  geom_line(data = alk |> filter(sample == "Integrated", !is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3)), aes(group = site), linewidth = .4) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1), guide = "none") + labs(x = NULL, y = "Alkalinity (mg/L as CaCO₃)", colour = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
int <- alk |> filter(sample == "Integrated", !is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3))
ph_d <- ph |> filter(depth_m <= 2) |> group_by(date) |> summarise(ph = mean(ph))
jj <- inner_join(filter(alk, !is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3)), ph_d, by = "date")
r_pa <- cor(jj$ph, jj$alkalinity_mgl_caco3, method = "spearman")
```

- **The lake is poorly buffered.** Integrated-sample alkalinity has a median of `r r2(median(int$alkalinity_mgl_caco3))` mg/L as CaCO₃ (range `r r2(min(int$alkalinity_mgl_caco3))` to `r r2(max(int$alkalinity_mgl_caco3))`) over `r nrow(int)` monthly samples (both sites combined) between `r min(int$date)` and `r max(int$date)`. Such low alkalinity lets pH move easily with photosynthesis, respiration and alum addition.
- **Alkalinity varies a lot from month to month**, with no regular seasonal cycle visible in about two years of monthly data.
- **Hardness and DOC are measured about once a year** (July or August, 2011 to 2017). DOC is low (`r r2(min(alk$doc_gm3, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(alk$doc_gm3, na.rm = TRUE))` g/m³) and hardness is steady (`r r2(min(alk$hardness_mgl_caco3, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(alk$hardness_mgl_caco3, na.rm = TRUE))` mg/L as CaCO₃).
- **No clear same-day link with pH.** Matching the `r nrow(jj)` alkalinity samples to the old buoy's 1 to 2 m pH on the same date gives a Spearman correlation of `r r2(r_pa)`. The sample is small, and alkalinity is only available while the old buoy was running (2015 to 2018), so it says nothing about the 2022 to 2026 pH decline.

### Do pH values exist on the sampling dates?

```{r}
#| include: false
chk <- alk |> mutate(has_ph = date %in% ph$date)
cnt <- \(v) { x <- chk[!is.na(chk[[v]]), ]; c(n = nrow(x), same_day = sum(x$has_ph)) }
cc <- sapply(c(Alkalinity = "alkalinity_mgl_caco3", Hardness = "hardness_mgl_caco3", DOC = "doc_gm3"), cnt)
no_ph <- chk |> filter(!is.na(alkalinity_mgl_caco3), !has_ph)
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Samples with a value for each variable, and how many have a buoy pH measurement on the same date."
knitr::kable(data.frame(Variable = colnames(cc), Samples = cc["n", ], `With pH on the same date` = cc["same_day", ], `Without pH` = cc["n", ] - cc["same_day", ], check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

Mostly, yes. `r cc["same_day", "Alkalinity"]` of the `r cc["n", "Alkalinity"]` alkalinity samples have a buoy pH value on the same date, all from the old buoy (the alkalinity file ends in February 2018 and the new buoy starts in February 2022). Of the `r nrow(no_ph)` without pH, `r sum(no_ph$date < as.Date("2014-02-25"))` were taken before the old buoy started on 25 Feb 2014, `r sum(no_ph$date > as.Date("2018-01-07"))` after it stopped in January 2018, and the other `r sum(no_ph$date >= as.Date("2014-02-25") & no_ph$date <= as.Date("2018-01-07"))` fall on days within the old buoy period when it has no pH record. Only `r cc["same_day", "Hardness"]` of the `r cc["n", "Hardness"]` hardness and DOC samples have a matching pH value. The old buoy measures at 1 m only, so each match is to surface pH, while the integrated samples cover a depth range.

```{r}
#| label: fig-alk-ph
#| fig-cap: "Same-date surface pH (old buoy, 1 to 2 m) against alkalinity at the two sites."
#| out-width: "60%"
ggplot(jj, aes(alkalinity_mgl_caco3, ph, colour = site)) + geom_point(size = 2) + labs(x = "Alkalinity (mg/L as CaCO₃)", y = "pH", colour = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Download

The raw, sub-daily pH record from both buoys (`r format(nrow(ph_raw), big.mark = ",")` rows), and the alkalinity, hardness and DOC samples, are available as CSV files. The figures and tables on this page use daily means in 0.5 m depth bins; the download is not averaged.

<a class="btn btn-primary" href="downloads/rotorua_ph_timeseries.csv" download><i class="bi bi-download"></i> Raw pH time series CSV (`r round(file.size("downloads/rotorua_ph_timeseries.csv") / 1e6)` MB)</a>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary" href="downloads/rotorua_alkalinity_hardness_doc.csv" download><i class="bi bi-download"></i> Alkalinity, hardness and DOC CSV</a>

pH file columns:

| Column | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `datetime` | Measurement time in NZST (UTC+12). New buoy: profiler readings about every 2.5 minutes; old buoy: every 15 minutes |
| `depth_m` | Sensor depth (m). New buoy: depth of the profiler at the reading; old buoy: fixed at 1 m |
| `value` | pH (pH units) |
| `source` | `old buoy` or `new buoy` |
| `qc_in_range` | `TRUE` if 4 < pH < 11; no values are removed |

The alkalinity file (one row per sample) has `site_id`, `location`, `datetime`, `alkalinity_mgl_caco3`, `doc_gm3` and `hardness_mgl_caco3` (alkalinity and hardness in mg/L as CaCO₃; DOC in g/m³).
